newsitem.title: USA: Mass. lottery financing bids due Tuesday - report.
newsitem.headline: Mass. lottery financing bids due Tuesday - report.

text.p: Financing companies have until 1200 EST/1700 GMT Tuesday to submit bids to lend the Massachusetts Lottery Commission $70.8 million - more than twice what the Legislature approved - so it can upgrade its computer and software systems, the Boston Globe reported on Tuesday.

The computers, from GTech Holdings Corp and Digitial Equipment Corp will be paid for over 10 years under a tax-exempt lease purchase adding $22.7 million in borrowing costs, the newspaper said. The total cost will be $93.5 million - more than twice the $45 million appropriated by the Legislature in December 1993.

Lottery Director Samuel DePhillippo and Secretary of Administration and Finance Charles Baker promised the legislators in a letter that the additional costs would be made up through savings, especially in "the dramatic reduction of expenses related to the high cost of maintaining antiquated terminals," the newspaper said.

The Lottery is in negotiations with its workers represented by Service Employees International Union Local 254. Some 100 union members service the antiquated computers that the Lottery has been using for more than 15 years.
